text:
The gain errors point to the op-amp, not the resistors. Both gains are low by the same factor: a1 is 0.81× its ideal value (-1000/132529 ≈ -7.54e-3 vs. -6.126e-3 simulated) and a2 is 0.81× its ideal value (-2.418e-3 vs. -1.963e-3). A wrong resistor would affect only one gain, so the shared shortfall suggests reduced loop gain. The strongest DC symptom is the input pair. M2 is in weak inversion with a non-matching length (L=0.15 vs. M1's L=0.52), which pulls the tail node (oa_t) down to 0.237 V. That pushes the tail source M5 into triode, so the tail current is 27.7 µA instead of the ~41 µA its mirror ratio implies. The differential pair's asymmetry is the most likely corruption.

The imbalance drives M2 into weak inversion and drops the tail node oa_t to ~0.24 V, pushing tail M5 into triode. Tail current falls below its mirror-ratio value, reducing the op-amp's loop gain and causing both a1 and a2 to fall about 19% short of the ideal ratios. Restoring M2 to L=0.52 um (matching M1) should be the first fix."}
